class_guess: Bell eats counter: a phase defect walks a 1010 budget word away from a binary counter (digits 11/00); at the far end the counter's low digits are eaten
summary: A phase defect walks a 1010 word one pair per count; at the far end it eats 1-3 low digits of a binary counter.
mechanism: Tape between counts: M(a,X,b,N) = 0^inf 10^a X 10^b 011 B> 0 D(N) 11 0^inf. D(N) 11 is N in binary, low digit first, 1 = 11, 0 = 00 (the final 11 is the leading 1). X is a one-cell phase defect (an extra 1 or 0) in the 1010 word.

Each count adds 1 to N and moves the defect left (X=1 -> X=0 in place, X=0 -> X=1 two pairs left). When it falls off the far end (word 10^p, no defect: E(p,N)) a C/F sweep runs the whole word into the counter and eats its low end: N odd -> (N+1)/2, N = 0 mod 4 -> N/4, N = 2 mod 8 -> (N+6)/8, N = 6 mod 8 -> a two-defect transient ending in a quick second eat. The word gains 2 to 7+t pairs.

Eat to eat: p' = p+1+e+[p odd], N' = f(N)+p'+[p even] (e = 1,2,3 digits eaten); 6 mod 8: N = (2m+1)2^(t+3)-2 -> E(p+7+t, m+2^t+t+1), N = 16m+6 -> E(p+7, m+5). This equals the direct run at all 2,091 eats to 1e11 steps. Invariant p >= 20, 1 <= N <= 2p is kept by every branch (algebra; exhaustive for p <= 2000) and holds from E(21, 6) at step 3,097. No branch halts (the only halt, F0, needs a C/F sweep, and all 514 sweeps to 1e9 are eats), so the pseudo-random order of eat types needs no prediction: not a cryptid. Siblings: none.

template.diff: different table (no busycoq hand proof within 3 transitions; the distance-3 tables are decider proofs in Indv2.v and RWL_mod_v3.v)
template.note: Same architecture as BECv5 TM1 (and our W4-2): a binary counter BinInc plus a budget word with a one-cell phase defect (TM1's R n m = 1 (10)^(1+n) 0 (10)^m), one budget pair per count (RIncs), an eat that removes low counter digits (ROv), BigStep and progress_nonhalt_cond with a linear invariant (TM1: a <= 1+b; here N <= 2p). Different: the defect walks AWAY from the counter and the eat happens at the far blank end via a C/F sweep over the whole word; the eat removes 1, 2 or 3 digits by N mod 8, plus a two-defect transient for N = 6 mod 8. Our counter D(N) 11 0^inf is BinInc [1;1] N on the right (RBinInc_spec).

strategy: S(p,N) := E(p,N). Prove INC1/INC0/INCL (E/B sweep, defect fix, A sweep, RBinInc_spec), the C/F sweep, EAT1-3 and EAT4 plus its transient, then BigStep E -> E. Close with progress_nonhalt_cond, P := p >= 20 /\ 1 <= N <= 2p, after multistep_nonhalt to E(21, 6) at step 3,097.
risks: The N = 6 mod 8 transient (a 1^(2t+1) block becomes a second defect that walks 2^t+t pairs and cancels the first) is validated end to end but its inner steps are not yet stated as exact lemmas; it is the largest piece of Rocq work.
No busycoq file has a defect that walks away from the counter with an eat at the far blank end, so most lemmas are new; expect a W4-2-sized effort (2-3 Rocq stages).
Edge cases must be exact: the defect at a = 0 or 1, a leading blank when p+7 = 2^t, and the [p odd] / [p even] terms in every eat.

status_reason: Mechanism closed: all 2,091 eats from blank to 1e11 steps follow the validated eat-to-eat model, and a simple linear invariant (N <= 2p) is kept by every branch. Next: proof.md, then Rocq from BECv5 TM1's architecture.
